adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin, vinblastine, and bleomycin (PVB) significantly prolongs the disease-free survival of patients with NSOCT of testis, Stages I or II, and that this treatment has no adverse effect on the patients’ fertility or sexual function.
adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin, vinblastine, and bleomycin (PVB) for patients with Stage I and II NSCT is effective in preventing relapse and prolonging survival.

there is no clear evidence that chemotherapy is of benefit for patients with Stages I and I1 NSGCT.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been unable to demonstrate that adjuvant chemotherapy in patients with Stage I or II NSGCT improves survival or relapse rate.

the results with adjuvant chemotherapy in Stages I and 11 NSGCT are not as good as those with adjuvant therapy in Stages III and IV disease, but they are better than those with surgery and/or radiation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the current adjuvant chemotherapy for testicular cancer, which is cisplatin, vinblastine and bleomycin (PVB), does not work very well for the patients who have a high risk for relapse, and we have shown that the combination of etoposide and cisplatin (EP) is better for them.
there is a need to develop a more effective adjuvant therapy, and that the best way of doing that is to have a better understanding of what’s going on at the tumor site.
